title: Add incident remediation SLA policy evaluator (due times + breach classification)
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes: Adds a small library + CLI for computing remediation SLA due timestamps and evaluating breach status based on incident severity, tier, and incident_type/subtype. Intended to be called by incident-bot and alerting pipelines; no customer-facing changes.
description: Context: As part of the Reliability Program (Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping), we need a single, audited implementation for remediation SLA timers. Today, multiple systems (incident-bot, dashboards, ad-hoc scripts) are calculating “SLA due” inconsistently, and edge cases (pause/override, force majeure, customer-caused) are handled differently. This PR introduces a small, dependency-light library in slo-toolkit to: (1) compute due_at for remediation SLAs from incident metadata, (2) evaluate whether an incident is currently in breach / at risk, and (3) provide a stable, versioned policy surface we can share across services. Scope / Approach: - Adds @redwood/sla-policy (library) with a compact policy model that takes severity (Sev0–Sev3), tier (Hosted | Dedicated | Private), and taxonomy (incident_type + optional subtype) and returns: time_to_mitigate_minutes, time_to_fix_minutes, due_mitigate_at, due_fix_at, and breach status given timestamps. - Includes a CLI tool `sla-policy` for debugging and validation (used by SRE during rollout + backfills). - Policy is defined as a checked-in JSON allowlist (low-cardinality, v1 taxonomy only) to avoid runtime lookups and to ensure “unknown/unclassified” behavior is explicit. - Supports pause windows and overrides via an optional `adjustments` array (e.g., pause from incident_start->provider_outage_resolved). These are treated as auditable inputs; the evaluator does not infer pauses. - Adds explicit handling for: unknown incident_type, missing tier, and “customer-caused” incidents (requires an explicit flag; otherwise default policy applies). Key API: - `computeSla(incident, policy, now)` returns `SlaResult`. - `evaluateBreach(slaResult, now)` returns `ok | at_risk | breached` with remaining_minutes. - `validatePolicy(policy)` is run at startup/CLI and in CI to prevent unbounded growth and to ensure all keys match the v1 taxonomy allowlist. Example: `const r = computeSla({ incident_id: "INC-24891", started_at: "2026-02-02T19:22:00Z", severity: "SEV1", tier: "DEDICATED", incident_type: "capacity", subtype: "regional_gpu_shortage" }, defaultPolicy, new Date());` returns due timestamps aligned with the remediation SLA matrix, and then `evaluateBreach` provides `at_risk` vs `breached` given the current time. Notes / Alignment: - Policy values and key names align with Confluence “Owner mapping + remediation SLA matrix” and the incident-bot required taxonomy fields rollout. - This evaluator is used by downstream work (redwood PR-28635 breach alerting + incident-bot gating) to ensure consistent SLA timers across systems. Testing: - Unit tests cover due time computation, pause/override windows, unknown keys defaulting behavior, and a set of golden test vectors derived from 8 real incidents (anonymized) from the last 90 days backfill. - Adds a policy validation test that fails CI if new policy keys are added without updating the allowlist + docs. Rollout plan: - Land library first; consumers will vendor it via semver tag from slo-toolkit. - SRE will run CLI against a sample of recent incidents to verify due_at matches the matrix before enabling breach paging. - Follow-up will wire incident-bot to show due_at and “time remaining” in the incident channel header.
commits: feat(sla-policy): add policy model + TypeScript types
feat(cli): add sla-policy CLI (compute + validate + explain)
test(sla-policy): add golden vectors + pause/override coverage
chore(ci): run policy validation in PR checks
docs: add usage examples + integration notes for incident-bot/alerts
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we confirm this won’t introduce metrics label cardinality issues? We should be careful about letting arbitrary incident_type strings into the evaluator output.

Aisha Bello: Good call. The evaluator only accepts incident_type/subtype that match the taxonomy allowlist; otherwise it returns `UNKNOWN` and uses the explicit default SLA. Also, `explain` output in the CLI is not intended for metrics labels—consumers should label only with the canonical incident_type enum (which already matches the allowlist). I added a test that ensures unknown keys don’t get echoed back as “normalized” labels.
Rafael Mendes: Two questions: (1) For Dedicated Sev1, do we distinguish mitigate vs fix? (2) What’s the behavior if started_at is missing (created_at vs declared_at differences)?

Aisha Bello: (1) Yes—policy returns both time_to_mitigate and time_to_fix. Consumers can alert on either; incident-bot will display both. (2) If started_at is missing we fail validation (throws) by default; there’s an optional `fallback_started_at` knob in computeSla() for ingestion pipelines that only have created_at. I added docs + tests and kept the default strict so we don’t silently shift timers.
Devon Price: For incident-bot integration we need a stable JSON output and a single command to compute due_at. Can the CLI output machine-readable JSON without extra text?
Aisha Bello: Added `--json` flag to `sla-policy compute` that emits a single JSON line (no surrounding logs). Also added `--quiet` to suppress validation warnings when running in bots.
Dylan Brooks: Looks good. Minor: please align severity naming with incident-bot (“SEV0” not “P0”). Also, can we add a short note about pause windows needing an audit trail?

Aisha Bello: Updated the enum names to SEV0–SEV3 and added a README note: pause/override inputs must come from an auditable source (incident timeline annotations or approved overrides), evaluator stays pure/deterministic.
Allison Grant: Approving. Thanks for adding the allowlist guardrail.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. Please link this in ENG-4829 so breach alerting consumes the same library.
